title: an external project's later round rebuilds a conflicting branch on its base and force-pushes it with a lease to the same PR, exactly like a self round, when the project's confirmed conventions allow force_with_lease; round 1's merge-commit catch-up is removed
acceptance: Why. 2026-10-06 ~01:45, the pilot external repository (external project the pilot external project, base master) PR #1 (branch t-002-work, head 1f038ee, review round 2 APPROVED) became CONFLICTING after the captain pushed master 8a4f393 and 1601a1e (main.cjs and styles.css). bring_up_to_date (bin/fm-worker.sh:1059-1063 on main) returns at once for FM_EXTERNAL=1, and the push block (bin/fm-worker.sh:2121-2124) exits 65 'task force-push needs confirmed project policy', so no round can bring an external branch up to date; the T-002 round 3 worker answered WORKER_BLOCKED / ASK-MERGE-PREPARATION. Round 1 of this PR answered with a merge-commit catch-up. On its merge card (D-firstmate-workflow-T223-2, 2026-10-06) the captain refused a merge commit in an external branch and then chose 'rebase on the same PR and force-push' (captain 2026-10-06): an external branch is rebuilt on the base exactly like a self branch and pushed with a lease on the same PR.

Mechanism. The self rebuild (bring_up_to_date at bin/fm-worker.sh:1059-1146 on main: rebuild_rebases probe, ls-remote lease, detach at the base, squash the old head in, conflicts listed for the worker, the commit, refs/fm-rebuilt/<branch>, push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<lease>, rebuild_settle) becomes the external path too. design §15.6 (design.md:5159-5160) already says 'A task-branch force-with-lease requires confirmed project policy and expected old head'; this task implements that sentence: an external rebuild runs only when the project's confirmed conventions say `force_with_lease: true` (read with `fm_stack_policy force_with_lease`, bin/lib/fm-stack.sh:29, which already returns the external conventions field through fm_conventions), and its expected old head is the PR head the round was bound to. With `force_with_lease` false, missing or unreadable, external behaviour is unchanged from main: the round is not rebuilt and nothing is force-pushed.

End state relative to main (c00e5cf), so the PR's diff is only what this task needs. Every piece of round 1's merge catch-up is removed: the function `external_catch_up`; `catchup_settle` and every call to it (the exit path near :232/:354/:625 and the push block); the ref namespace `refs/fm-caughtup/`; the variables `caught_up`, `catchup_prev`, `catchup_base`, `catchup_head` and every branch that tests them (prompt block, worker_changed_files, the pre-commit checks, new_scripts_executable call, the commit-tree two-parent commit path with `commit_parents`, the push/settle branch, the `caught_up` event data in `rebuild_args`); the `catchup` argument of `rebuild_side_left` and `rebuild_collect_conflicts` (return those to main's inline form or keep a refactor only if the self path still uses it unchanged in behaviour); the MERGE_HEAD refusal added to bin/fm-checkpoint.sh; the gate 2 ancestor shortcut in bin/fm-gate.sh; the stub lines added only for the catch-up in tests/conventions-publication.test.sh (`catchup_settle() { :; }`) and the `rebuild_publishes() { return 1; }` stubs round 1 added to tests/external-review-launchers.test.sh and tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh, together with any post_note / rebuild_publishes change that made them necessary — every stub returns to main's set exactly (main's own stub at tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh:165 in test_external_question_is_not_a_draft_candidate stays). After this round bin/fm-gate.sh, bin/fm-checkpoint.sh, tests/conventions-publication.test.sh and tests/external-review-launchers.test.sh are byte-identical to main, and `git grep -nE 'merge --no-ff|commit_parents|fm-caughtup|caught_up|catchup' -- bin` is empty (main's single-parent `commit-tree` commit of the self rebuild at bin/fm-worker.sh:2091 and its comments stay). Kept from round 1: nothing else; the braced-variable fixes go away with the lines that needed them. Kept from main: everything in the self rebuild path, unchanged in behaviour.

Change 1, bin/fm-worker.sh bound head. At :630-632 (main) the external PR check `fm_binding head --task "$TASK" --pr "$PR" --branch "$branch" >/dev/null || exit 65` keeps its refusal but stores the head it prints: `bound_head="$(fm_binding head …)" || exit 65` (declare `bound_head=''` before :630, beside `leftover_dirty=0` / `branch_existed=0` at :573-574 — not with the rebuild variables at :939-941, which run after the binding — so self rounds and external rounds with no PR read an empty value under set -u).

Change 2, bin/fm-worker.sh bring_up_to_date (:1059-1063 on main). The FM_EXTERNAL early return is replaced by: for FM_EXTERNAL=1, (a) `fm_stack_policy force_with_lease` must print exactly `true`; any other answer, or a failure, prints 'fm-worker: the project conventions do not allow force_with_lease; <branch> is not rebuilt / 專案慣例不允許 force_with_lease；不重建 <branch>' (variables braced, e.g. ${branch}) and returns 0 with nothing changed, the same as main's hold; (b) an external round with no open PR (`$PR` empty) is not rebuilt (returns 0 with 'fm-worker: no open PR; <branch> is not rebuilt this round / 沒有開啟的 PR；本輪不重建 <branch>'). Then the existing self body runs unchanged for both kinds (clean-tree check, fetch of +refs/heads/$BASE into refs/remotes/origin/$BASE, merge-base, rebuild_rebases probe — a branch that still rebases cleanly is left alone exactly as for self —, the ls-remote lease, the ancestor check). One extra external check right after the lease is read: when FM_EXTERNAL=1 the lease must equal `$bound_head`; otherwise print 'fm-worker: origin's <branch> is not the head this round was bound to; not rebuilding it / <branch> 並非本輪綁定的版本；不重建' and return 0. `rebuild_entry` stays self-only (:1118); `rebuild_own_file_restore` and `rebuild_lost` keep their behaviour (an external task file is private and never in the branch). The rebuilt-round prompt's task-file paragraph (bin/fm-worker.sh:1364-1369 on main: 'Your task file design/tasks/<id>.json must come through exactly …', both the pinned and the unpinned form) is printed only when FM_EXTERNAL=0; an external rebuilt prompt names no design/tasks path.

Change 3, bin/fm-worker.sh push block (:2112-2145 on main). The `if [ "$FM_EXTERNAL" = 1 ]; then … exit 65; fi` refusal is replaced by external publication checks before the leased push: `fm_stack_policy force_with_lease` is read again and must print `true` (else the same exit 65 with message 'fm-worker: the project conventions do not allow force_with_lease; rebuild retained for recovery / 專案慣例不允許 force_with_lease；保留重建結果以便復原'), `$rebuild_lease` must be non-empty and equal `$bound_head` (else exit 65, 'an external branch that is not the head the round was bound to'), and fm_publication_policy's checks run for the rebuilt tree. fm_publication_policy (bin/fm-config.sh:1109-1121) reads the branch from `symbolic-ref HEAD`, which fails while the rebuilt tree is detached; give it an optional second argument, the branch name to check, used instead of symbolic-ref when given (`fm_publication_policy "$tree" "$branch"`), so the protected-base refusal (main|master|HEAD|$FM_BASE) and the worktree/common-dir checks still run. The push itself is main's line unchanged: `git -C "$tree" push -q --force-with-lease="refs/heads/$branch:$rebuild_lease" origin "$rebuilt_head:refs/heads/$branch"`, with main's refusal path (rebuild_settle, exit 71) and main's success path (checkout -B, branch -u, clear refs/fm-rebuilt). The PR keeps its number: the later-round path that posts `commit_pushed --pr "$num"` with `rebuild_args` (rebuilt data, once) runs as for self; no new PR is created and none is closed. The post-push rebuild note on the PR (bin/fm-worker.sh:2203-2218 on main, `fm_github pr comment "$num"` with the previous head, new head and conflicts) runs only when FM_EXTERNAL=0. For FM_EXTERNAL=1 the same three facts are kept privately instead with `fm_private_note` (kind `rebuild`, the task, a file holding the same text), the way external reports are kept (bin/fm-worker.sh:1651-1660); nothing about the rebuild is posted to the external PR.

Change 3b, the heads an external rebuilt round reports. `round_head` (bin/fm-worker.sh:1228) is read after bring_up_to_date has detached the tree at the base, so in a rebuilt round it is the base tip. For FM_EXTERNAL=1 and rebuilt=1: the context pack (`--head` at :1247), the external prompt identity ('Checkout/head SHA' at :1271) and the private worker report saved right after the adapter returns (`fm_evidence report --head` at :1620, still saved first, before publication) all use `$rebuild_prev`, the bound PR head the round started from. The early projection inside `post_note` (`fm_external project --head "$round_head"` at :1656, reached from :1875 before the commit) is skipped in an external rebuilt round; the existing after-push projection at :2236-2241 (`--head "$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse HEAD)"`) is the one that runs, with the pushed head that bin/lib/fm_external.py:234-236 checks. Self rounds and external rounds that were not rebuilt are unchanged.

Change 4, the message at :1061 'external rewrites require the explicit restack helper and expected-head lease' and the one at :2122 'task force-push needs confirmed project policy; rebuild retained for recovery' no longer exist in bin/; grep bin/ and tests/ for both strings and update every assertion that names them. bin/lib/fm-stack.sh, bin/lib/fm_stack.py (restack still requires `force_with_lease: true` and `stacking: allowed`, :89 and :234) and bin/lib/fm_autopilot_branches.py / bin/lib/fm_autopilot.py (:378) are read and left unchanged: stacking and autopilot restacks keep their own rules; say so in the PR.

Exit codes: no new code. 65 keeps 'external policy refused' and 'an unverifiable external PR head'; 71 keeps 'the leased push was refused'. Every new bilingual message braces each variable that is followed by non-ASCII text (the non-ASCII variable-boundary lint, bin/ci.sh:613-619).

Tests (fail-first; workers do not run suites; CI and the gates verify; fail-first runs only *.test.sh). Rework tests/worker-external-catchup.test.sh (the PR's new suite; keep its fixture harness: a local bare origin, an external FM_HOME with CONVENTIONS.md, a stub adapter, the real bin/fm-worker.sh) to the rebuild behaviour, every case its own assertion: (1) force_with_lease true, PR open, branch conflicting with the base: the round rebuilds — the prompt names the conflicting files, after the stub worker resolves them origin's branch is a single commit whose parent is the base tip, the push was `--force-with-lease=refs/heads/<branch>:<bound head>`, no `pr create` ran, the round's events carry the `rebuilt` data exactly once, no `pr comment` ran, a private `rebuild` note holds the previous head, and the rebuilt-round section of the prompt the stub adapter received (from '# Your branch was rebuilt', bin/fm-worker.sh:1322-1374) contains no 'design/tasks/' (the worker skill file that heads every prompt may still name it); this case is red on base (main holds every external rebuild). (2) force_with_lease false: not rebuilt, the policy message is printed, origin's branch is unchanged, no force push ran. (3) a function-level case with `fm_stack_policy` stubbed to fail: `bring_up_to_date` holds the branch exactly as in (2) (a conventions file with the field missing is rejected at startup by bin/fm-worker.sh:52 with exit 65 and origin unchanged, which the suite may also assert end to end). (4) origin's branch moved after binding (lease != bound head): not rebuilt, origin unchanged. (5) the push is refused because origin moved between the rebuild and the push: exit 71, origin unchanged, the local branch still at the previous head, and refs/fm-rebuilt/<branch> cleared by rebuild_settle as on main (bin/fm-worker.sh:303-317). (6) a branch that still rebases cleanly: nothing rewritten, origin unchanged. (7) a static assertion that `git grep` of bin/ finds none of 'merge --no-ff', 'commit_parents', 'fm-caughtup', 'caught_up'. (9) an external rebuilt round's context pack, prompt identity and private report name the previous PR head; the early projection in post_note does not run, and the after-push projection names the pushed head (no 'projection head is stale' failure). (10) an external rebuilt round that exits with a dirty tree publishes nothing: `publish_wip_if_dirty` (bin/fm-worker.sh:232-249) reaches its rebuilt branch and prints 'the rebuild … was not committed; nothing is published'. (8) fm_publication_policy with an explicit branch argument refuses main, master and $FM_BASE on a detached tree. Update tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh `test_external_rebuild_is_held_and_never_reads_public_spec` (main :152-160): with force_with_lease false the external rebuild is still held and the push block still refuses (exit 65 with the new message), and no public spec is read in either case. Names of helper functions in the suite must not start with `assert_` unless tests/lib.sh defines them (bin/ci.sh:1134-1153).

Callers checked: `bring_up_to_date` is called only at bin/fm-worker.sh:1146 (round_two). `fm_publication_policy` is called at bin/fm-worker.sh:232 (publish_wip_if_dirty) and :2146 (the fast-forward push), and wherever else `git grep -n fm_publication_policy` finds it; the fast-forward push keeps one argument and today's behaviour; publish_wip_if_dirty passes `"$branch"` as the new second argument so an external rebuilt (detached) tree reaches its own `rebuilt` check at :249 and publishes nothing, instead of failing at symbolic-ref (bin/fm-config.sh:1119). `fm_stack_policy` callers (fm-worker.sh:550, fm-gate.sh, fm_stack/autopilot) are unchanged; `rebuild_settle` callers are unchanged. `fm_binding head` callers are bin/fm-worker.sh:631, bin/fm-external.sh:29, bin/fm-gate.sh:162, bin/fm-review.sh:303 and bin/lib/fm_autopilot_loop.py:122; only the fm-worker.sh call site changes (it now keeps the output).

Design (edit in place, no new section at the end, T-189). design/design.md §5.3.3 'A later round starts from the current base' (design.md:930-1054): replace round 1's external catch-up paragraphs with one paragraph after the whole rebuild description saying that an external round uses the same rebuild only when the project's confirmed conventions set `force_with_lease: true`, that the lease is the PR head the round was bound to, that the rebuilt branch is pushed to the same PR with --force-with-lease and never to a protected base, and that with `force_with_lease` false the branch is held as before (captain 2026-10-06, D-firstmate-workflow-T223-2). §15.6 (design.md:5159-5160) gains one clause after 'requires confirmed project policy and expected old head': '(an external rebuild, T-223: conventions `force_with_lease: true`, expected old head = the bound PR head)'. skills/firstmate/SKILL.md:1045 'External stacking/rebuild remains held for T-143.' becomes 'External stacking remains held for T-143; an external rebuild runs only when conventions set force_with_lease: true, force-pushed with a lease on the bound PR head (T-223).' skills/worker/SKILL.md: remove round 1's catch-up text; the rebuild text at :100-123 applies to external rounds too, and its self-only sentence about the frozen task entry stays self-only.

Migration / in flight: nothing stored changes format. the pilot external project's CONVENTIONS.md says `force_with_lease: false` and its captain intent says 'no force push'; T-223 does not change it. Before T-002 (PR #1) can be rebuilt, the captain confirms a conventions change to `force_with_lease: true` through the normal conventions review (design §15.2); until then T-002 stays held exactly as today. Self rounds are unaffected.
Out of scope: stacked-PR restacks (fm-restack.sh, fm_stack.py), autopilot update-branch, landing/merge, conventions contents of any project, the self rebuild path's behaviour.

Scope. bin/fm-worker.sh, bin/fm-config.sh (fm_publication_policy optional branch argument only), bin/fm-gate.sh and bin/fm-checkpoint.sh (back to main only), tests/** (tests/worker-external-catchup.test.sh, tests/onboarding-crew.test.sh, and returning tests/conventions-publication.test.sh and tests/external-review-launchers.test.sh to main), design/design.md, skills/firstmate/SKILL.md, skills/worker/SKILL.md, design/tasks/T-223.json. Any other file needing a change: stop and name it.
